ledger_events.query: Inspect the three GeoPackage inputs, identify their layers, geometry types, CRS, relevant attribute fields, and spatial extents. Confirm which layer contains hospital points, Centre County tract polygons, and county subdivision boundaries. Report any data quality issues relevant to creating a hospital-count choropleth.

Retrieve and inspect the remaining input GeoPackages. Identify layers, geometry types, CRS, relevant fields, and spatial extents for hospital points and county subdivision boundaries. Also verify whether the previously retrieved Centre County tracts dataset is usable for spatial aggregation.
Retrieve fx_hospitals_utm.gpkg specifically and inspect its available layer(s), geometry type, CRS, fields, and extent. Return the retrieved artifact path and identify the hospital point layer.

The requested hospitals file was not returned; an unrelated DEM was returned instead. Please locate and retrieve the exact file named fx_hospitals_utm.gpkg from the supplied inputs. Do not substitute another dataset. Return its artifact path, layer name(s), geometry type, CRS, fields, and feature count.

Search the available input workspace for the exact filenames fx_hospitals_utm.gpkg and fx_county_subdivisions_utm.gpkg. Retrieve both exact GeoPackages (not DEM or other substitutes), list their layer names and metadata, and return artifact paths. If either file is unavailable, explicitly report that exact filename as unavailable.

Create the hospital-count choropleth workflow using the supplied GeoPackage inputs. First locate/load the exact files fx_hospitals_utm.gpkg, fx_tracts_centre_utm.gpkg, and fx_county_subdivisions_utm.gpkg if accessible. Use Centre County tract polygons as the choropleth units, spatially join hospital points to tracts, count hospitals per tract (including zero-count tracts), and optionally overlay county subdivision boundaries for context. Preserve or harmonize CRS as needed. Return the output choropleth vector artifact path, layer name, CRS, hospital-count field, and a concise summary of counts and any issues. Do not substitute the DEM or unrelated data.

Validate the vector_analysis_a result and independently produce the correct hospital-count dataset. Inspect the available exact GeoPackages and confirm that Centre County tract polygons are the aggregation units and hospitals are point features. Perform a point-in-polygon join, count hospitals per tract including zero counts, retain tract identifiers and geometries, and optionally include subdivision boundaries only as a separate context layer. Return the resulting choropleth-ready vector artifact path, layer name, CRS, count field, tract count, total hospital count, and min/max counts. Do not use intersection output as the final result unless it is demonstrably the correct tract-level aggregation.

Inspect the vector_analysis_b artifact and verify whether it is a valid tract-level hospital-count dataset. Report layer schema, geometry type, CRS, number of tract polygons, hospital_count field values including zeros, total hospital count, and whether all Centre County tracts are represented. If valid, provide the artifact path and statistics for map styling; if invalid, explain the defect.

Create the final choropleth map from the vector_analysis_b artifact, using Centre County tract polygons symbolized by hospital_count with a sequential color ramp and a clear legend/title. Include zero-count tracts, use an appropriate map extent, and overlay county subdivision boundaries only if available and valid. Inspect the input first; if it is not a complete tract-level polygon dataset, use the best valid tract-level aggregation artifact available from vector_analysis_a or vector_analysis_b and report the limitation. Return the rendered map artifact path and, if possible, a map-ready vector layer path.
